A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COPE study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 report original planning and benchmark experiments. Appendix A adds ablations, sensitivity analyses, latency measurements and repeated-run results.

after.justification: Sections 3 and 5 retain the original empirical evaluations, and Appendix A.1 retains the ablations, sensitivity analyses, latency measurements and repeated-run results.

M1.justification: The three-stage planner–executor procedure, goal/guideline distinction, plan reuse, confidence-based escalation and task-specific adaptations are unchanged. Revised introductory descriptions do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: MATH-500, AIME-2024, MBPP with MBPP-ET hidden tests, MT-Bench and ALFWorld. No dataset, task domain or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: Cascade, including its mathematical vote/verify variants, ABC, FrugalGPT and the applicable small-model and large-model controls. Comparator membership and model pairings are unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated splits, model configurations, sampling settings, thresholds and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both versions already describe MT-Bench win rates and ALFWorld success rates in prose; v4 changes the table headings without revising those evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Stage truncation, difficulty breakdowns, sample-count and threshold sensitivity, latency analysis and qualitative examples are retained. The empirical appendix moves from Appendix A to A.1 without adding or removing analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations over five independent runs with different random seeds. Table 13 and its reporting practice are unchanged; the explanatory subsection moves from A.6 to A.1.6.

E6.justification: Matched result tables retain all numerical entries and the prose findings. Tables 6–7 are relabeled without changing their numbers. The MT-Bench discrepancy also persists: Section 5.3 reports 36.9% COPE wins, whereas Table 6 contains 44.8%.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), the consensus definition and the latent-variable, Bayesian and mixture-of-experts interpretations are retained. Appendix B becomes A.2; mathematical differences are typesetting and reference-format changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free, few-shot-free collaboration through planning and reduced API cost with comparable or better performance across the same task domains. Abstract and contribution-list revisions preserve these claims.

C2.justification: The dedicated Limitations section is removed, including the learned-router qualification and escalation-related latency explanation; the appendix latency discussion remains. The accessibility argument in Broader Impact is also removed, and the introduction stops explicitly equating model size, cost and strength.

D1.justification: Hardware, batch sizes, decoding temperatures, API model versions, prompts and the statement that code is supplied in supplementary material are unchanged. Newly printed bibliographic URLs already existed as embedded links in v3.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against independent cascades, single-model compute scaling and earlier planning approaches are retained. Introductory rephrasing and bibliography formatting do not establish new research positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited abstract, introduction and contribution rewrites, author/affiliation updates, section deletions including the AI-use disclosure, and a new appendix hierarchy. Most prose and the main section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two columns to one, with revised typography, figure/table placement and table captions moved above their displays. All five figures and fifteen tables are retained. Table 6 changes its heading from Success rate to Win rate, while Table 7 makes the reverse change.

improvement.justification: V4 uses more careful size/cost wording and aligns Tables 6–7 headings with their captions, but removes the explicit learned-routing limitation and AI-use disclosure. The latency analysis remains, and the MT-Bench prose/Table 6 discrepancy is unresolved. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these opposing reporting gains and losses do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
